description:
Converge the GF(2) elimination family: give `ordered_column_elimination` a blocked (M4RI-style) schedule so the unblocked ordered loop stops being a third elimination path beside the blocked left-to-right and unblocked right-to-left `rref` variants.

## Background

`ordered_column_elimination` (crates/gf2-core/src/alg/rref.rs) is a deliberate, tracked exception to @/inv/convention-convergence: the blocked `rref` schedule assumes ascending pivot columns (suffix-only block updates, contiguous pivot-bit fast path), so it cannot host an arbitrary preference permutation, and neither existing path tracks a row transform. Equivalence distance is already measured: ordered elimination under natural order reproduces `rref(a,false)` exactly and under reversed order matches `rref(a,true)` up to row order (crates/gf2-core/tests/ordered_column_elimination.rs). `rref` sits on a benchmark-receipted hot path, so convergence must not regress it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One elimination mechanism serves ordered-preference and directional pivoting, or the blocked ordered schedule shares its block kernels with `rref` with no third independent loop.
- [hard] REQ-02: Existing `rref` benchmark receipts are reproduced or re-baselined under the named benchmark protocol with no regression outside noise.
- [hard] REQ-03: The ordered-elimination conformance suite passes unchanged.
- [aspirational] REQ-04: Transform accumulation gains a blocked schedule with measured elimination counts.
title: Blocked schedule for ordered-column elimination
